definitions.explanation: A subjective sensation or feeling, especially a physical or emotional state of comfort or discomfort. Most commonly used as a suffix in compound words describing how something feels.

examples.japanese: {住|す}み{心地|ごこち}のいい{部屋|へや}だ。
examples.english: It's a comfortable room to live in.
examples.notes: When used as a suffix, the reading changes to ごこち.

examples.japanese: このソファは{座|すわ}り{心地|ごこち}がいい。
examples.english: This sofa is comfortable to sit on.

examples.japanese: {春風|はるかぜ}が{心地|ここち}よく{頬|ほお}を{撫|な}でた。
examples.english: A spring breeze pleasantly caressed my cheeks.

notes:
USAGE:
Rarely used as a standalone noun in modern Japanese. Most commonly appears as a suffix （〜{心地|ごこち}） attached to verb stems to express how something feels to do: {乗|の}り{心地|ごこち} (ride comfort), {着|き}{心地|ごこち} (wearing comfort), {寝|ね}{心地|ごこち} (sleeping comfort). When used as a suffix, the reading changes to ごこち through rendaku.

The adjective {心地|ここち}よい (pleasant, comfortable) is also common.

COMPOUNDS:
- {住|す}み{心地|ごこち}: comfort of living (in a place)
- {座|すわ}り{心地|ごこち}: sitting comfort
- {着|き}{心地|ごこち}: wearing comfort
- {乗|の}り{心地|ごこち}: ride comfort
- {寝|ね}{心地|ごこち}: sleeping comfort
- {心地|ここち}よい: pleasant, comfortable
